text:
Maya: FYI we got a customer escalation from a Dedicated tenant (customer: Zephyr) — they see sustained 429s and spikes in tail latency across their inference pool starting ~08:20 UTC. Logs show a lot of eviction churn and KV pressure warnings. Noticed during a long-context batch job run.

Priya: Thanks, Maya. Can you paste the log snippet + which pool/zone? We should include tenant id and pool id for SRE routing.

Maya: Pool: dedicated-us-west-2-pool-12, Tenant: zephyr-prod-42. Log excerpt below:

```
2026-03-17T08:21:03Z WARN kv_cache: eviction: evicted=1234 free=16MB total=768MB
2026-03-17T08:21:03Z WARN kv_cache: fragmentation=0.78, allocator_failures=12
2026-03-17T08:21:04Z ERROR request: id=req_0x9a3b ttl=120ms serve_delay=230ms status=429 reason=kv_pressure
2026-03-17T08:21:05Z INFO autoscaler: scale_event=noop reason=threshold_violated_but_nodes_full
```
\nMaya: Also seeing many long-context requests (seq_len ~32k) from a small subset of keys.

Ravi: Assigning to eng-sre to investigate noisy-tenant + autoscale behavior. @Jonah can you look at runtime side? The autoscaler log line `nodes_full` + allocator failures suggests fragmentation preventing new KV allocations, so existing nodes don't accept new requests and autoscaler thinks capacity is saturated.

Jonah: Looking. Quick hypothesis: long-context workloads increase per-request KV footprint and fragmentation — leads to many small evictions and allocator churn. If the runtime's memory arena fragments, free contiguous space may be insufficient to allocate large KV pages, even if aggregated free memory looks ok. Autoscaler sees high queueing/latency and marks pool saturated, but new nodes are rejected due to config or boot throttles.

Priya: Customer reports they started a large batch migration job at 07:58 UTC which lines up. Repro steps from their side: 1) Send 2k long-context requests in parallel (seq len > 16k) targeting chat-model-x, 2) Observe rising 429s after ~10 minutes.

Ravi: Can we collect `rdwctl node inspect` output for the pool and the kernel allocator stats? Also heap fragmentation metrics and per-node KV cache occupancy.

Maya: Collected outputs and pasted to support log:

```
rdwctl node inspect --pool dedicated-us-west-2-pool-12 --json
# summary
nodes: 8
nodes_with_high_kv_pressure: 3
avg_kv_frag_ratio: 0.74
allocator_failures_last_5m: 38
boot_pending_nodes: 1
```
\nMaya: Container IDs for hot nodes: node-12-3b9f, node-12-4a1d, node-12-8c2e.

Jonah: Thanks. Short-term mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase pool min capacity (force immediate additional nodes), 2) rolling restart of affected nodes to free fragmented arenas, 3) apply a per-tenant rate-limit/quota to the offending tenant to reduce parallel long-context traffic. I recommend 1+2 together for quick relief and 3 for safety.

Ravi: If we do rolling restarts, we need to drain connections gracefully to avoid request loss. Also check whether autoscaler has a cooldown misconfig that prevented adding nodes earlier.

Priya: Customer wants a quick fix. Can we do a one-time capacity bump? I can authorize up to +4 nodes under emergency process.

Jonah: I'll run a light-touch script to trigger scale and compact KV on new nodes:

```
# trigger scale
rdwctl pool scale --pool dedicated-us-west-2-pool-12 --add 4 --reason "emergency-eviction-burst"
# on each new node (automated via init hooks):
rdwctl runtime kv-compact --node $NODE_ID
```
\nJonah: Also set a temp tenant throttle rule: `tenant:zephyr-prod-42 -> max_concurrent_long_ctx=50` (applied in routing layer).

Maya: Executed the scale command at 08:26 UTC. New nodes are provisioning; alerts-bot shows new nodes created: node-12-9f7a, node-12-a31b, node-12-b8e1, node-12-c0d3.

alerts-bot: pool_event: added 4 nodes to dedicated-us-west-2-pool-12 (ids: node-12-9f7a,node-12-a31b,node-12-b8e1,node-12-c0d3).

Maya: After compact + drain on two hot nodes and applying throttle, error rate dropped from ~18% 429s -> ~1.2% over next 8 minutes. Latency tail improved from 1.1s -> 220ms p95 for typical requests.

Ravi: Good. Still want to understand root cause: why fragmentation was so high. Can we get allocator metrics pre/post-compact (arena_count, bin_utilization, largest_free_block)? Also check kernel selection; large seq lengths may be triggering a fallback path that allocates large contiguous KV chunks.

Jonah: Noted. I'll pull allocator histogram and a memory map for the decommissioned nodes. Early glance shows many small freed blocks and only few large contiguous blocks. Also found that a recent runtime change to KV LRU bucket sizing reduced coalescing — filing a follow-up PR to revert adjustable bucket sizing.

Priya: Action items:
- Jonah: attach allocator histograms, memory maps, and PR link to the ticket (eta 6h).
- Ravi: review autoscaler cooldown + node boot failure reasons (eta 3h).
- Maya: coordinate with Zephyr CS, confirm temporary throttle, and keep monitoring.

Maya: Zephyr confirmed reduced failure rate and accepted temporary throttle while we investigate.

Ravi: Marking this thread as escalated -> eng-runtime + eng-sre. We'll keep this open until root cause PR is merged and we've done a follow-up runbook update for long-context noisy tenants.

Jonah: Logged issue INF-9872 "KV arena fragmentation during long-context workloads" with initial repro and mitigation steps.

Maya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Priya: Closing customer-facing loop, will update Zephyr with mitigation summary and next steps.

Ravi: If anything regresses ping me directly.
